lesson.scenario: A sequencer assigns global slots to concurrent commands so replicas apply one identical total order.
entities: Submits command X without coordinating with B
Assigns the next unique monotonically increasing slot
Applies only the next contiguous slot
connections: append command at assigned global slot

steps.title: A submits concurrent X
steps.narration: A sends X while the sequencer next slot is 81.
steps.outcome: X is proposed but has no globally visible position yet.
steps.invariant: Proposal arrival alone does not define total order; only a unique assigned slot does.

steps.title: B wins the next slot
steps.narration: B proposal Y reaches the sequencer before queued X and receives slot 81.
steps.outcome: Concurrent real-time proposals are deterministically ordered Y before X.
steps.invariant: Each slot is assigned to at most one command.

steps.title: X receives the following slot
steps.narration: The sequencer assigns X slot 82 and appends it after Y.
steps.outcome: The authoritative total order is now [Y, X].
steps.invariant: The log order is a strict sequence even for commands that were concurrent.

steps.title: Replica buffers an out-of-order slot
steps.narration: R2 receives slot 82 before 81 and holds X; R1 receives and applies slot 81.
steps.outcome: R2 does not let transport reordering change the sequenced order.
steps.invariant: A replica applies only its next expected global slot.

steps.title: Replicas converge on one order
steps.narration: R2 receives slot 81, applies Y, drains buffered X, and matches R1 after R1 applies 82.
steps.outcome: Both replicas expose the identical sequence Y then X.
steps.invariant: Total order requires all correct replicas to place every delivered command in the same relative position.

production.scenario: A flash-sale inventory system totally orders reservation commands for one SKU so hundreds of checkout pods cannot oversell the last few game consoles.
components: Submit reserve commands for SKU 441 from many web servers at once
Owns sellable-inventory decisions for flash-sale SKUs
Assigns one position to every reservation and release command
Authoritative ordered inventory history for SKU 441
Turns accepted ledger entries into pickable stock allocations
Rebuilds the SKU ledger by replaying the ordered command stream
flows: Dozens of checkout pods race to reserve the same console while stock is nearly exhausted.
submit reservation command for total ordering
The reservation service does not mutate stock directly until the command has a global position.
The sequencer places the reservation into one ordered stream that becomes the only authoritative history for the SKU.
apply ordered reservation and remaining stock
The allocator decrements sellable quantity in command order and rejects any reservation beyond zero.
Each checkout pod learns whether its hold won only after the ordered ledger has applied the command.
replay ordered command stream after failover
If the inventory ledger is rebuilt in another zone, disaster recovery replays the same ordered commands and reaches the same remaining stock.
